transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-10
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Kapoor (Redwood SE), Noah Diaz (Redwood CSM), Lena Ortiz (Cerulean Head of Data), Markus Voss (Cerulean CTO), Priya Shah (Cerulean ML Eng), Ethan Cole (PM)

Summary:
High-level scoping for a 4-week pilot to validate generation quality for financial summarization and downstream accounting ingestion. Focus: define golden prompts/golden set, regression cadence, hallucination / numeric-format checks, scoring weights, success thresholds, and bench workload sizing.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Um, quick roll call, and then, uh, we'll jump into the acceptance criteria.
[00:06] Lena Ortiz: Hi, Lena here. Thanks Maya.
[00:08] Markus Voss: Markus on the call.
[00:10] Priya Shah: Hey, Priya.
[00:12] Ethan Cole: Ethan here.
[00:14] Ravi Kapoor: Ravi from Redwood. Noah's also on.
[00:16] Noah Diaz: Hey all.
[00:22] Maya Chen: Awesome. The goal for today is to nail down what success looks like for the POC — golden prompts, what we'll use to run regressions, the hallucination checks especially for monetary values, and how we score everything, right. I'll hand it to Priya to give a quick problem statement from Cerulean's side.
[00:35] Priya Shah: Sure. So our main use case is auto-summary of transaction threads for our corporate banking product. We want the model to extract amounts, counterparties, and the required next action. Downstream systems ingest the output, so format matters a lot. If the model invents a number or puts a Euro sign when we expect USD that's a critical fail. Also performance matters — we need near real-time for the UI.
[01:02] Maya Chen: Perfect, that helps. When we say "format matters a lot" — can you quantify? Like percentage of perfect-format outputs?
[01:08] Priya Shah: Right now, we're aiming for 98% format correctness for amounts and dates in the golden set, and less than 2% hallucination on monetary amounts across the golden set. Latency target is p95 under 400ms for front-end flows, but for blob-backend batch jobs p95 can be up to 1.2s.
[01:28] Ravi Kapoor: Okay, cool. The way we've run similar pilots: we ask for a 200-query golden set that represents typical live traffic, plus a longer regression set of ~1k examples that capture edge cases, high token counts, malformed receipts, currency conversion noise, etc. We then run a baseline with your current model and a candidate open model on Redwood Hosted and Redwood Dedicated to compare.
[01:46] Markus Voss: Quick question on dedicated vs hosted: what's the realistic perf delta? We've seen other vendors claim big differences.
[01:53] Ravi Kapoor: Yeah so, um, dedicated hardware eliminates noisy neighbors and lets us pick quantization strategies — in practice we've observed p95 wins of ~150–300ms on sequence lengths typical for you, but it depends. Also Dedicated gives more consistent throughput. Note: I might have said "KV cash" earlier in docs, it's "KV cache" — transcript auto sometimes swaps it.
[02:12] Lena Ortiz: Good to note. On scoring — we want a combined score but also per-dimension thresholds. What dimensions do you recommend?
[02:18] Maya Chen: Our recommended scoring breakdown for generation acceptance:
- Accuracy / Entity extraction (amounts, counterparties): 40% weight
- Format & schema adherence (amount format, currency code, date ISO): 25%
- Hallucination penalty (invented amounts or fabrications): 20% (we treat hallucination as a hard penalty in scoring)
- Safety / PII redaction checks: 5%
- Latency & stability (p95 latency and error rate): 10%

[02:46] Priya Shah: That seems reasonable. For hallucination as a "hard penalty", how does that work in practice?
[02:51] Ravi Kapoor: Practical approach: any time the model outputs a monetary amount that is not present in the source and there's no clear derivation, we flag it as hallucination. For scoring we subtract a fixed penalty per hallucination instance, and set an absolute pass condition: hallucination rate on the golden set must be <= 2%. If hallucination rate is between 2-5% we can consider remediation steps; above 5% it's a fail.
[03:14] Ethan Cole: Do we also differentiate between format errors and hallucinations? Like a wrong currency symbol vs made-up number.
[03:19] Maya Chen: Yes. Format errors are separate — they reduce the format score but don't always trigger the hallucination penalty unless the number itself is fabricated. So output "$1,234.00" vs "1.234,00€" — second is wrong format but not necessarily hallucinated.
[03:36] Lena Ortiz: OK. What's the evaluation process? Manual annotation? Automated checks?
[03:40] Ravi Kapoor: Combination. We'll run automated validators for schema & regex checks (amount patterns, ISO dates, currency codes). For hallucination detection and entity correctness we recommend a sampled manual review — maybe 10% of the golden set with human labels plus automated diff for the rest. That keeps cost reasonable. We'll also seed the regression harness with annotated golden answers for exact match / normalized numeric compare.
[04:01] Priya Shah: On sample size — is 200 golden prompts enough for statistically meaningful results?
[04:06] Ravi Kapoor: For core acceptance gates, 200 well-chosen golden prompts is usually sufficient to validate basic quality and catch major regressions. For more fine-grained metrics and confidence intervals, the 1k regression set helps. If you want p-values for small deltas, we'd bump samples, but for a POC 200/1k is a common tradeoff.
[04:24] Markus Voss: Benchmarks — what metrics will you run and what's the deliverable?
[04:29] Maya Chen: We'll provide a benchmarking report with p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput qps at target concurrency, token-level cost estimate, and the full evaluation matrix: per-prompt result, normalized numeric diff, format pass/fail, hallucination flags, and aggregate weighted scores. We'll also include exportable CSVs and a short deck with run notes.
[04:48] Ethan Cole: For throughput sizing — we expect peak UI bursts around 40 QPS and background jobs at about 10 QPS over long tails. Is that something Redwood can simulate?
[04:57] Ravi Kapoor: Yes. For the bench-run we'll run three profiles: interactive burst (40 QPS, low tokens), mixed (15 QPS, variable tokens), and batch (10 QPS with high token counts). We'll simulate KV cache warm/cold scenarios too. Again note: tokenization differences across models can affect p95.
[05:15] Priya Shah: About hallucination checks: sometimes the model converts currencies implicitly — we want to avoid that. Can we enforce no implicit conversions?
[05:23] Maya Chen: Yup, we'll include prompt templates and system instructions to tell the model not to perform conversions unless asked. Those templates will be part of the golden prompts. And we'll add an automated rule: if output contains a numeric value with a currency that doesn't match the source currency, mark it as format or hallucination depending on context.
[05:40] Lena Ortiz: Timeline? We need to sync with internal budget and compliance windows.
[05:43] Noah Diaz: Proposed timeline from Redwood:
- Week 0 (this week): finalize golden prompt template and shared sample set
- Week 1: Cerulean provides 200 golden + 1k regression examples; Redwood prepares bench harness and pre-configures Hosted and Dedicated variants
- Week 2: Run baseline and candidate model bench; deliver draft evaluation report
- Week 3: Remediation + targeted prompt tuning and re-run critical failing cases
- Week 4: Final report and acceptance decision; optionally plan for Dedicated onboarding if pass criteria met

[06:14] Markus Voss: That aligns with our internal quarter end; we need results before Dec 15.
[06:18] Maya Chen: Sounds doable. Success criteria recap — let's put hard numbers on this so everyone is clear:
- Weighted aggregate score >= 0.85 (85%) across golden set
- Entity extraction accuracy (amount + counterparty) >= 90%
- Format correctness >= 98% on amounts/dates/currency codes
- Hallucination rate <= 2% on golden set (hard pass)
- P95 latency for interactive flow <= 400ms on Dedicated; Hosted should be within 1.5x of that as a reference
- Error rate (timeouts/500s) < 0.2%

[06:49] Priya Shah: I'm comfortable with those thresholds, provided we get the remediation loop and retesting baked in.
[06:55] Maya Chen: Right — remediation plan: after baseline run we'll prioritize top 20 failing prompts, try prompt variants, then if needed we can test a quantized variant or a different model variant. We'll capture experiments in the runbook.
[07:09] Ethan Cole: For regression cadence post-POC — we want a weekly smoke-run and a monthly full regression. Is that supported?
[07:15] Ravi Kapoor: Yes, Redwood Optimize can schedule weekly smoke tests (a subset of critical prompts) and monthly full runs. For Dedicated customers we can automate and store pinpoints, diff alerts, and golden-set drift alerts.
[07:28] Lena Ortiz: Any security/compliance blockers we should flag now? KMS, log retention, PII handling?
[07:33] Noah Diaz: We'll send the security pack (SOC2 docs, data flow, retention options). For pilot we can keep all data in isolated buckets and redact PII at ingestion; Redwood Private or Dedicated has KMS integration if you need customer-managed keys. I'll attach the checklist.
[07:50] Markus Voss: Good. One more: can we capture per-field confidence so our downstream can decide when to ask for human review?
[07:57] Ravi Kapoor: We can return token-level logprobs or model confidence signals; we also recommend a heuristic: normalized numeric diff < threshold maps to high confidence. We'll include prob/exposure in the evaluation records.
[08:10] Priya Shah: About data retention during pilot — how long do you keep logs?
[08:14] Noah Diaz: Default retention is 30 days for pilot logs, but we can extend or configure S3 sink to your environment. For private deployments data never leaves your VPC.
[08:25] Maya Chen: OK, let's close with explicit next steps and owners. We've captured action items in the doc but to restate: Maya will send the golden prompts template and sample rubric by Friday; Priya will upload 200 queries by next Wednesday; Ravi will schedule the bench-run and share the config; Noah will send security pack. We'll reconvene after the baseline report — tentatively Nov 23 for results review.
[08:49] Lena Ortiz: Great, thanks everyone.
[08:51] Markus Voss: Thanks.
[08:53] Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up.

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hears: "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "KV cash"; model names sometimes appear truncated in auto-caption, please rely on attachments for exact config.
